blocks.content: In English, modifiers can appear on either side of a noun. In Japanese, they always come *before* the noun they describe : adjectives, relative clauses, and entire subordinate phrases all stack up before their noun.

rows.japanese: 田中さんが作ったケーキ

blocks.content: Relative clauses in Japanese require no relative pronoun : no "that", "which", or "who". You simply place the entire clause before the noun: 昨日読んだ stacks directly onto any following noun.
